# Independent audit of the one-parity full-body depth loss

Audited `candidate ace4ff0d14f43769` in full and
reran `supporting computation verify_one_parity_condition_depth_loss.py` with plain Python.
**PASS; no correction needed.** The full-dimensional tube and its
intrinsic coarse/fine measure conventions are essential and are
correctly retained throughout the statement.

The integer crosspolytope bases are exactly zero and the signed
coordinate vectors. The affine parity graph has heights one half
at zero and zero or one at the other bases. The strict condition
epsilon less than one half therefore removes exactly the zero
coarse base under fine sampling, without creating endpoint fibers.
All fine positive fibers are copies of the same simplex, and the
coarse fibers are intervals times that simplex with equal volume.

At the proposed coarse center, every through-point scalar margin
splits into the centered simplex projection plus independent
symmetric noise. The archived paired-centroid-tail theorem applies
to each nonzero simplex normal, including atomic noise. For zero
simplex normal, closed symmetry gives at least one half. The
canonical simplex caps cover the entire body and each has coarse
fraction Gamma_s, so the global coarse maximum is exactly Gamma_s.
This upper bound holds at every admissible point, not merely at
the proposed center.

For each signed coordinate base, its exposing functional has gap
at least one to every other positive base. The coefficient two in
the displayed fine caps therefore strictly excludes all other
fibers even when the simplex coordinate reaches one. At the own
base the cap is precisely a canonical simplex cap. The resulting
finite cap cover gives the global upper bound Gamma_s/(2m), and
the ordinary centroid theorem in any single actual fine fiber
gives the matching lower bound for every ambient cap orientation.

The projected common-space total variation is exactly
1/(2m+1), with the convention of supremum over measurable sets.
This concerns the projected normalized laws only: the original
coarse and fine measures have different intrinsic dimensions.
The lost coarse central point is no longer fine-admissible, so
fixed-domain depth continuity is not being contradicted.

The affine fine lattice is correctly identified by
2u minus the sum of p coordinates equal to one. Its projection is
the odd-sum coset, with even-sum direction lattice of index two
and rank m. The convex hull of the fine source is exactly the
graph of the affine parity function times the simplex. It has
codimension one in the full tube. The note explicitly preserves
this failure of the exact-fine-hull hypothesis and does not claim
an OC counterexample.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
